title: Protocol for deciphering the electrical parameters of perovskite solar cells using immittance spectroscopy
protocol: Ultrasonicate substrates in 2% Hellmanex solution for 20 minutes at 30°C.
Wash substrates with deionized water.
Ultrasonicate substrates in acetone for 20 minutes at 30°C, repeat if necessary.
Treat cleaned ITO substrates with UV-Ozone for 30 minutes.
Stir PEDOT:PSS solution for approximately 30 minutes.
Filter stirred PEDOT:PSS solution through a 0.22 μm nylon filter before use.
Place 50 μL of PEDOT:PSS solution on the center of the ITO substrate.
Wait for ~3 seconds to allow the solution to spread over the substrate.
Spin-coat the substrate at 5,000 rpm for 30 seconds with an acceleration of 2,500 rpm/s.
Prepare the PTAA solution with a concentration of 5 × 10−3 g/mL in toluene.
Stir the PTAA solution at 22°C–25°C for 2 h in glove box.
Cast 50 μL PTAA solution in the center of the ITO substrate.
Spin-coat at 5,000 rpm for 30 s with acceleration (2,500 rpm/s).
Anneal the PTAA film at 100°C for 5 min.
Reconstitute 1 M PbI2 (600 mg/mL) in 1 mL dimethyl formamide (DMF).
Stir the PbI2 solution at 70°C for 12 hours at 400 rpm/s.
Dissolve MAI and MACl (50:5 mg/mL) in 1 mL IPA at 22-25°C.
Stir the mixed organic cation solution at room temperature for 12 hours at 400 rpm/s.
Prepare a PC61BM solution with a concentration of 10 mg/mL in chloroform.
Stir the PC61BM solution at room temperature for 2 hours.
Prepare a BCP solution with a concentration of 0.5 mg/mL in IPA.
Stir the BCP solution at room temperature for 24 hours.
Filter the PbI2 solution through a 0.45 μm PTFE filter.
Keep the filtered PbI2 solution at 70°C for further use.
Filter the mixed organic cation solution through a 0.45 μm PTFE filter.
Cast 30 μL hot PbI2 solution on the center of ITO/HTL and spin-coat at 4500 rpm for 20 s with acceleration (9,000 rpm/s).
Cast 50 μL mixed organic cation solution dynamically on the wet PbI2 film without stopping.
Continue spin-coating at 4500 rpm for 30 s after dynamic casting of mixed organic cation solution.
Anneal as-prepared film at 100°C for 5 min.
Cast 60 μL PC61BM solution on perovskite film and spin-coat at 1500 rpm for 30 s with acceleration (750 rpm/s).
Control the temperature of the glovebox below 30°C during PC61BM electron transporting layer preparation.
Increase concentration of PC61BM in chlorobenzene or toluene to 20 mg/mL for spin-coating on perovskite film at 4000 rpm for 30 s.
Leave as-prepared PC61BM film for around 2 h in the glovebox or keep it in vacuum condition for more than 30 min for solvent volatilization.
Cast 60 μL BCP solution on top of PC61BM film and spin-coat at 4000 rpm for 30 s with acceleration (2,000 rpm/s).
Remove perovskite film marked by a red rectangle in Figure D using a cotton bar with DMF.
Clean samples with an air gun to dry solvent residues and remove dust particles before placing into the substrate holder for evaporation.
Control the rotation speed of the substrate holder at 20 rpm/s during the evaporation process.
Calibrate the light illumination using a standard Silicon (Si) cell.
Place the standard Si solar cell at the center of the simulated xenon light source, aligning it to the same height as the devices.
Adhere the shadow mask to the un-encapsulated solar cells to define an active area of 0.09 cm².
Measure J-V curves under reverse scan from 1.2 V to -0.1 V at a scan rate of 100 mV/s, with a delay time of 100 ms and pre-sweep delay of 10 seconds.
Perform C-f measurements at variable temperatures using a Keysight precision LCR meter linked to a Linkam heating/cooling stage filled with liquid nitrogen.
Cool down the devices to 150 K.
Start measurements in the heating mode from 150 K to 350 K.
Place the sample inside the Linkam heating/cooling stage.
Connect the probes to the top and bottom contact of the device.
Check the connectivity using a multi-meter.
Fill the liquid nitrogen in DF2 Flask.
Set the desired temperature using the temperature controller with a ramp rate of 2°C/min.
Wait for 3–5 minutes after reaching the desired temperature to stabilize.
Measure the capacitance in the frequency range from 100 mHz to 2 MHz.
Repeat the measurements at different temperatures.
Check the VOC of the device under illumination if high variation is observed in measured spectra.
Replace the device if there is over a 5% change in VOC.
Carry out impedance measurements in the desired frequency range using a Biologic SP300 Potentiostat.
Illuminate the device with a white LED at controlled light intensity ranging from 0.1 to 0.5 sun illumination.
Use a faradaic chamber for sample measurements to minimize noise and external interferences.
Measure impedance under short circuit conditions.
Turn on Biologic SP 300 Potentiostat.
Wait for 30 minutes to stabilize the system.
Place the sample inside the faradaic cage.
Connect the device electrodes with Biologic SP 300 Potentiostat.
Open EC Lab software.
Load settings for Potentiostatic Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (PEIS).
Set Ewe to E = 0 V vs. Ref.
Set scan frequency from fi = 2 MHz to ff = 0.1 Hz, with Nd = 10 points per decade in Logarithm spacing.
Set AC perturbation Va = 20 mV.
Wait for pw = 0.1 s period before each frequency measurement.
Average measure per frequency Na = 2 and corrects the drift of the system.
Record the impedance spectra in dark.
To record IS under illumination, vary the current of LED.
Record the illumination intensity via Lux meter.
Measure J-V before and after IS measurement.
If there is a variation of more than ±5% in VOC, replace the device.
Vary Ewe to E = 0.2 V to 0.8 V and keep other parameters as above.
Measure J-V after IS measurement under open circuit condition.
Record the IS in dark as well as under illumination.
AC perturbation has to be high enough to produce a noise-free signal but small enough to ensure linearity.
Increase AC perturbation or integration time, and/or increase the number of Integration cycles during measurement.
Maintain Vac such that it does not affect the linearity of the signal.
Give a 2−5 min interval between successive measurements for stabilization of mobile ions.
Identify the measuring frequency from the stable plateau region of C-f spectra.
Measure in single “single sine” mode using EC Lab software.
Set scan voltage from −0.5 V to +1 V with adequate number of points.
Choose scan frequency based on the identified measuring frequency from C-f spectra.
Set AC perturbation Va = 20 mV.
Wait for pw = 0.1 s before each frequency measurement.
Average measurements per frequency Na = 2 to correct system drift.
Record Mott-Schottky plot.
Perform the measurement at low temperature where all ionic motion is diminished if a linear region in the Mott-Schottky plot is not visible.
